title: Robot Corset Catapult Physics Lab
description: A robot stands on a seesaw-style catapult platform. The user configures launch parameters (angle, spring force, spin rate) to fling a corset through the air and land it on a series of floating target pedestals. Realistic projectile physics with gravity, air drag, and angular momentum govern the trajectory, and the robot animates to stomp the catapult lever on launch.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a physics catapult mini-game. Load robot.glb and Corset.glb via GLTFLoader from 'shared_assets/'. Scene setup: a ground plane with grid texture, a seesaw catapult built from BoxGeometry planks with a pivot at center-left. Place the robot on the heavy end (right side) and the corset on the launch cup (left side). Add 3 floating target pedestals (CylinderGeometry, glowing rings) at varying distances (8, 15, 23 units) and heights (2, 5, 3 units). Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,8,-18) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: DirectionalLight with shadows, HemisphereLight for ambient fill. UI panel (HTML overlay, top-left) with: (1) launch angle slider 15-75 degrees, (2) spring force slider 5-30 N, (3) spin rate slider 0-10 rad/s, (4) air drag coefficient slider 0.01-0.5, (5) target selector dropdown for pedestal 1/2/3, and a LAUNCH button. On launch: animate the robot stomping down (rotate robot -30deg over 0.3s), the seesaw pivots, and the corset launches as a projectile. Simulate physics each frame: apply gravity (-9.81 m/s²), quadratic air drag (F_drag = -0.5 * Cd * v²), and spin the corset around its forward axis at the configured spin rate. Draw a trailing line (BufferGeometry) showing the trajectory path. On landing (corset y <= pedestal top y within pedestal radius), flash the pedestal green and show 'HIT' with distance error in meters. If it misses and hits the ground, flash red and show 'MISS'. Track attempts and hits in a scoreboard. Add a RESET button to return corset to catapult. Validate all parameters: angle must be number in range, force must be positive, drag coefficient must be > 0. Show warning text if invalid. The robot should have idle animation (gentle bobbing) between launches. Scale the corset to roughly 0.4 units and the robot to 2 units tall. Ensure shadows are enabled on all meshes.
